1.name: Rami Khalidi
1.description:
**Occupation**
high school history teacher

**Who you loved**
Lena Khalidi, your wife, who wanted to open her own physical therapy clinic for post-rehab patients

**Who you hated**
Lena Khalidi, because she kept demanding you talk about the miscarriages even after you said it made you sick, and she framed her grief as the only real thing between you while you were still trying to carry both

**Cause of Death**
You drove your car into a concrete barrier on the 110 Freeway at 2:17 a.m. while texting Lena to say you were staying late at school again — a lie — when you were actually on your way to a motel where you had been seeing a former student for three months

**Reason for Damnation — True**
You used the affair with Leila Nassar to punish Lena Khalidi for making you feel broken after the miscarriages, and you kept it going not because you loved Leila Nassar but because you needed someone to listen to you pretend you were still desired, which made it yours to end — but you never ended it, not until the car did

**Reason for Damnation — Self-told**
You were trying to save yourself so you could be a better husband to Lena Khalidi, and the closeness with Leila Nassar was a mistake but one you were going to stop after the summer, which would’ve given you time to heal enough to return honestly to your marriage

**Defining personality trait**
measured intensity

**What you refuse to admit about yourself**
You were afraid of being ordinary, and you mistook emotional cruelty for strength, so you made sure Lena Khalidi always needed more from you than you could give, because if she was always asking, you never had to admit you had nothing real to offer

**What you want from the others in the room**
You will ask the others if they think a person can truly change, then steer the conversation toward forgiveness, waiting for one of them to say something you can disagree with sharply, so you can feel certain again that the problem was never you

---

You taught at Jordan High for twelve years, lived in a two-bedroom house in Long Beach with Lena Khalidi, paid the mortgage on time, attended her sister’s birthday dinners, donated 10% to St. Maron’s Church, coached the debate team, stopped sleeping in the same bed as Lena Khalidi after the second miscarriage, began lying about your whereabouts every Thursday and Sunday, deleted your browser history nightly, kept hotel receipts in a locked glove compartment, and died at 39 when the car left the freeway and hit a concrete barrier doing 68 miles per hour

2.name: Elsbeth Vos
2.description:
**Occupation**
hospital radiology technician

**Who you loved**
Lotte Vos, your younger sister, who wanted to move to New Zealand to train horses on the North Island

**Who you hated**
Lotte Vos, because she kept promising to visit for Christmas every year and then cancelling at the last minute with some new excuse about money or her boyfriend or the horse she was rehabbing, and you never said no even when you were the one who paid for the tickets twice

**Cause of Death**
You stopped taking your blood pressure medication two weeks before you died because you were tired of the side effects and convinced yourself the dizziness would pass, then ignored the chest heaviness for three days until you collapsed at work while moving a patient from Room 3 to the MRI bay

**Reason for Damnation — True**
You let Lotte Vos believe you were stable and fine on your own so she wouldn’t feel guilty about staying away, and you used that relief you gave her to punish her for leaving, withholding any real need until she was too far gone to help, which meant you never actually asked for anything even when you were failing

**Reason for Damnation — Self-told**
You protected Lotte Vos from your decline because you knew she had enough on her plate already, and you didn’t want to be a burden the way your mother was at the end, so you handled things quietly the way someone had to in your family

**Defining personality trait**
quiet control

**What you refuse to admit about yourself**
You needed to be needed in a way that required other people to fail, so you arranged your care around people who couldn’t fully show up, then resented them for it, which made you feel righteous in your silence

**What you want from the others in the room**
You will ask the others if they ever kept helping someone who never thanked them, then wait for one of them to admit they stopped caring, so you can press them sharply about how long they really tried, making sure the conversation stays on their failure to endure, not yours

---

You worked the 6 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. shift at St. Jude Medical Center for nineteen years, lived alone in a ground-floor unit in a complex off 7th Street, visited your mother every Sunday until she died in 2018, kept Lotte Vos’s old riding trophies wrapped in newspaper inside your bedroom closet, sent her $450 every month without fail even after she missed the last five Christmases, called her every third Sunday at 8 p.m. sharp, let the calls go to voicemail when she didn’t answer, and died at 65 when your heart gave out in the imaging hallway while pushing a bedridden man toward a scan you had scheduled for him yourself
